jobs.excerpt: Grafana Labs, the company behind the open observability cloud, is founded on the principles of open source, open standards, open ecosystems, and open culture.
jobs.description:
Grafana Labs, the company behind the open observability cloud, is founded on the principles of open source, open standards, open ecosystems, and open culture. Grafana Cloud, our fully managed observability platform, is flexible and built for scale. With Grafana Cloud's actually useful AI, organizations can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data to move at the speed of their ambitions. Today, more than 35 million users and 7,000+ customers – including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce – trust Grafana Labs to ensure reliability of their applications and systems, resolve incidents quickly, and optimize their telemetry to reduce noise and cost. We are a 100% remote company with 1,600+ team members across 40+ countries, and we’re backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

Senior Software Engineer - k6 Core

The Opportunity:

At k6, we build reliability and performance testing tools for developers and QA engineers.

Grafana k6 is an open-source project focused on making performance testing practical, approachable, and useful in real-world engineering workflows. We care deeply about developer experience, correctness, and scalability. k6 is part of the Grafana ecosystem and is used by engineers to test and understand systems under real load.

What You’ll Be Doing:

You will join a team of engineers responsible for building and maintaining k6, a performance testing tool written in Go. The team also maintains the open-source project, which means working directly on the product, the codebase, and with the community using it.

In this role, you will work on features and improvements across the k6 codebase, from initial idea through implementation and delivery. Much of the work involves problems that are not fully specified up front and require understanding the context, evaluating trade-offs, and choosing a reasonable technical approach.

You will work with a high degree of independence while collaborating closely with other engineers on design, implementation, and code reviews. You are expected to deliver production-quality code, maintain existing functionality, and help keep the system reliable and maintainable over time.

Some work may involve the k6 cloud offering, which builds on top of k6 to run distributed tests across data centers worldwide. This includes Go services that support distributed execution and require careful attention to performance, correctness, and failure modes.

Because the team is small, your work will have a direct and visible impact on the product and its users. You will work alongside experienced engineers in an environment that values clarity, pragmatism, and sound engineering judgment.

We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction. We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups—always with strong code review and quality standards. You'll also have access to the latest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

We start with problems, not prescriptions. Engineers are expected to understand the constraints, propose a pragmatic design, and carry the work through to delivery. We move deliberately and release on a regular cadence of roughly every six weeks. Between releases, we focus on small, safe, incremental changes.

Work is asynchronous by default, with decisions captured in pull requests and short design notes. Meetings are used for alignment rather than status updates. Code reviews focus on correctness, long-term maintainability, and user impact. When trade-offs are required, we aim to make them explicit and reversible. The team owns the product end to end, including architecture, releases, user-facing behavior, and the health of the open-source project.

We’re looking for an experienced engineer with strong programming skills and a track record of working on non-trivial systems.

You should have:

  • Strong experience building production software in Go, or another language with good support for concurrency and parallelism
  • Experience working on larger or long-lived codebases
  • The ability to work independently on scoped problems and deliver them to completion
  • Clear technical communication skills, especially in code reviews and design discussions
  • A good understanding of internet protocols such as HTTP, gRPC, and WebSockets, with some familiarity with lower-level networking concepts
  • Experience with modern development practices, including testing, code review, and iterative development

Bonus Points For:

You do not need experience with everything listed below. These are areas where familiarity is useful for the role, and the more you bring, the easier the ramp-up will be:

  • Contributing to or maintaining open-source projects
  • Prior experience using k6 in production, or contributing to the k6 project or ecosystem
  • Performance, reliability, or network testing and optimization
  • Distributed systems or cloud-based services
  • JavaScript and/or TypeScript
  • Backend systems for web or mobile applications
  • Tools and platforms such as Docker, AWS, microservices architectures, and observability tools like Grafana or APM systems

Compensation & Rewards:

In Sweden, the Base compensation range for this role is SEK 775,444- SEK 930,533. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer:Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow.

jobs.description:
Job Purpose:

The Odoo Accountant is responsible for managing the full accounting cycle of the company through the Odoo ERP platform, ensuring accurate financial recording, compliance with Saudi regulatory requirements (ZATCA, VAT, e-invoicing), and timely reporting. The role supports the growing technology portfolio across Customer Experience solutions, system integration projects, and enterprise IT services by maintaining robust financial controls, project-based accounting, and vendor/partner financial management (Genesys, Cisco, and other technology partners).

Key Responsibilities

  • Project & Contract Accounting:
    • Manage project-based revenue recognition, cost tracking, and profitability per engagement
    • Link sales orders, purchase orders, and timesheets to projects in Odoo
    • Monitor milestone-based billing (e.g., Genesys, Cisco projects)
    • Track deferred revenue for multi-year contracts
    • Generate project P&L reports for management
  • Compliance & Tax Management:
    • Ensure compliance with Saudi regulations (VAT, ZATCA, Zakat)
    • Handle VAT filings (monthly/quarterly)
    • Manage ZATCA Phase 2 e-invoicing (Fatoora) integration
    • Calculate withholding tax (WHT) for international vendors
    • Stay updated on regulatory changes and reflect them in Odoo
  • Financial Reporting & Analysis:
    • Prepare financial statements (P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow)
    • Support budgeting and forecasting cycles
    • Build dashboards for revenue performance by business line
    • Conduct variance analysis (actual vs. budget)
  • Accounts Payable & Receivable:
    • Manage vendor invoices and payment cycles (e.g., Genesys, Cisco, Microsoft)
    • Oversee collections and monitor aging reports
    • Follow up on overdue receivables
    • Handle multi-currency transactions (SAR, USD, EUR)
  • Internal Controls & Audit Support:
    • Maintain audit documentation and trails
    • Support external audits
    • Ensure segregation of duties within Odoo
    • Improve financial controls and approval workflows
  • Process Automation & Continuous Improvement:
    • Automate accounting tasks (recurring invoices, bank feeds, OCR)
    • Collaborate with IT on Odoo customizations and integrations
    • Identify and implement process improvements for efficiency

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field. Professional certifications (SOCPA, CMA, ACCA, or CPA) are highly preferred.

  • Experience: 3–6 years of hands-on accounting experience, with a minimum of 2 years working extensively on Odoo ERP (preferably Odoo 18 or later). Experience in technology, IT services, or system integration companies is strongly preferred.

  • Technical Skills: Deep working knowledge of Odoo Accounting, Invoicing, and Purchase modules; proficiency in Odoo configuration, reporting, and basic troubleshooting; strong Excel skills (pivot tables, VLOOKUP, financial modeling); familiarity with ZATCA e-invoicing integration and Saudi VAT framework.

  • Regulatory Knowledge: Solid understanding of Saudi accounting standards (SOCPA), IFRS, VAT regulations, Zakat requirements, and ZATCA Phase 2 e-invoicing compliance.

  • Languages: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken) is essential for handling local regulatory documentation and international partner communications.

They provide expert technical consultation, strategic advisory, robust cybersecurity defenses, scalable IT infrastructure, and advanced contact center technologies.

jobs.excerpt: ABOUT KALLES GROUP:Everyone deserves to be secure.
jobs.description:
ABOUT KALLES GROUP:

Everyone deserves to be secure. Our mission at Kalles Group is to help secure the future for companies of all shapes and sizes.

While our expertise spans multiple disciplines, our method remains consistent: building trust and relationship with people -- whether you are a client, a consultant, or--in this case--a candidate.

No matter what role you come from--whether you're an executive or just starting your career-you can expect our highest level of attention and respect. We want to find the right fit for each role, but we also want you to find the right fit for your career.

We believe the best way to show you what our team is like is to treat you like you're already a part of it. We hope you'll consider joining our team of experienced professionals who are building their careers at Kalles Group—and having fun while doing it.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

As a Principal IAM Engineer Consultant, you will provide senior technical leadership for our client's Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) platform, helping design and deliver secure, scalable identity capabilities that support millions of customer interactions within a highly regulated financial services environment. Serving as the technical authority across engineering, architecture, cybersecurity, product, and delivery teams, you will transform strategic identity initiatives into detailed engineering solutions while driving engineering quality and technical consistency across the platform.

This is a hands-on engineering leadership role—not a program management or governance position. You will author detailed engineering designs, define secure authentication and integration patterns, guide implementation teams, and help shape the long-term evolution of the organization's customer identity platform. Success requires deep expertise in modern consumer identity technologies, authentication protocols, cloud-native architectures, and the ability to influence technical direction through credibility, collaboration, and sound engineering judgment.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop engineering-level solution designs for CIAM initiatives, including architecture, integration patterns, data flows, security controls, operational readiness, and implementation sequencing
  • Partner with Product Owners, architects, cybersecurity teams, engineering, and delivery stakeholders to align technical solutions with business priorities
  • Coordinate technical delivery activities by managing dependencies, clarifying ownership, resolving blockers, and supporting predictable execution
  • Provide technical leadership and mentoring to engineering teams, reinforcing secure coding practices, documentation standards, and maintainable implementation approaches
  • Identify engineering risks, technical debt, architecture drift, and security gaps that could impact platform stability or delivery quality
  • Advise Product Owners on backlog sequencing, technical readiness, engineering complexity, and delivery trade-offs
  • Facilitate technical decision-making across multiple teams while building alignment on architecture, priorities, and implementation approaches
  • Support delivery governance by escalating recurring issues, monitoring execution quality, and partnering with leadership to resolve delivery challenges
  • Develop reusable design patterns, technical standards, implementation guidance, and delivery playbooks that improve consistency across the CIAM program
  • Document technical decisions, assumptions, risks, and mitigation strategies throughout the delivery lifecycle
  • Strengthen collaboration across engineering, cybersecurity, architecture, product management, and vendor partners to improve delivery outcomes
  • Develop detailed engineering design documentation—including authentication flows, integration patterns, sequence diagrams, token architecture, and implementation guidance—to enable consistent, secure delivery across multiple engineering teams.

ABOUT YOU:

Your values:

    • Integrity: You believe in doing the right thing, even when it's uncomfortable, seemingly inefficient, or costly.
    • Purposefulness: You have a desire to serve others with your skillset and an openness to continuous learning and growth.
    • Ownership: You stick to your commitments, follow up with action, and seek clarity in communication & expectations.

YOUR EXPERIENCE:

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of progressive software engineering or identity engineering experience, including significant time operating at a Senior, Lead, Staff, or Principal Engineer level
  • Deep hands-on expertise designing and implementing Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) solutions supporting customer-facing applications at enterprise scale
  • Expert knowledge of modern identity platforms including Ping Identity (PingFederate/PingOne), ForgeRock, Okta Customer Identity/Auth0, or Microsoft Entra External ID
  • Experience producing engineering-level design documentation including:
    • OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), and SAML federation
    • Authentication and authorization flows
    • Passwordless and MFA architectures
    • Session and token management
    • API security and integration patterns
    • Sequence diagrams, data flows, and implementation designs
  • Proven ability to influence architecture and engineering decisions across multiple delivery teams without direct management authority
  • Experience identifying technical debt, architecture drift, security gaps, and implementation risks while driving practical engineering improvements
  • Strong understanding of secure software engineering, Zero Trust principles, and cloud-native identity architectures
  • Experience supporting high-volume customer-facing identity platforms within banking, credit unions, insurance, fintech, or similarly regulated industries
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to build consensus across engineers, architects, product leaders, and executive stakeholders while navigating complex organizational environments

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading or supporting large-scale customer identity platform migrations, consolidations, or modernization initiatives
  • Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, or identity platform integrations across multiple organizations
  • Experience with Azure API Management (APIM), Cosmos DB, F5 Distributed Cloud/Shape, or similar supporting technologies
  • Experience integrating CIAM solutions with customer-facing mobile applications and digital banking platforms
  • Familiarity with fraud prevention and identity risk platforms such as Outseer
  • Experience creating reusable architecture patterns, engineering standards, and technical playbooks
  • Knowledge of Infrastructure as Code, cloud-native architectures, and DevSecOps delivery practices

WHAT WE OFFER:

jobs.excerpt: Who we are At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes.
jobs.description:
Who we are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.

.

Hiring and how we work :

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.

.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Principal Internal Communications Manager, a high-impact, individual contributor leadership role reporting to and working in close partnership with the Internal Communications Lead.

About the job

Twilio’s Internal Communications team is seeking an experienced, strategic, and highly collaborative Principal Internal Communications Manager to serve as a cornerstone of our global IC function. In this role, you will act as a primary thought partner to the team lead on overarching program strategy and execution, while taking direct ownership of our most critical, sensitive, and high-stakes employee communications. Your work will be integral to protecting Twilio's culture, aligning our workforce, and navigating complex corporate moments for our 5,500 Twilions around the world.

This Twilion will have world-class strategic acumen, impeccable discretion, and a calm, steady demeanor under pressure. You are a seasoned expert at navigating complex corporate, legal, and social environments, possessing the rare ability to translate high-stakes business realities into empathetic, clear, and highly effective internal narratives.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Partner on Global IC Strategy: Work in close partnership with the Internal Communications Lead to co-architect the overarching strategic direction and execution of the wider internal communications program.
  • Partner closely with PR/External Comms: Serve as point of contact with external comms team during strategic projects and crises, ensuring internal and external narratives stay aligned and sequenced.
  • Lead highly sensitive employee communications: Own the end-to-end strategy, narrative creation, and execution for high-stakes, sensitive corporate scenarios, ensuring absolute confidentiality, accuracy, and cultural alignment. Including but not limited to employment legal issues, ethics and misconduct cases, regulatory or legal actions, and safety & security incidents.
  • Manage transactional & structural change comms: Drive the internal communication strategy for complex corporate evolutions, including Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A), strategic transactions, organizational redesigns, and executive transitions
  • Advise on social Issues: Provide strategic counsel and develop thoughtful framework-driven messaging regarding complex external political and social issues, balancing company values with employee sentiment.
  • Collaborate cross functionally: Partner deeply with Legal, HR, Employee Relations, Security, and Corporate Affairs to operationalize communications around sensitive matters, ensuring a unified, legally compliant, and compassionate voice.
  • Support finance communications: Partner with the Finance org and ghostwrite for the CFO on both companywide financial moments (earnings, financial updates) and the CFO's internal comms to the finance org, including quarterly updates and finance org all hands.
  • Flex across the IC portfolio: When there isn’t an active strategic project or crisis, plug into the broader work of the team (Q&A prep, All Hands support, comms campaigns, etc.) and whatever else needs a strong writer and thinker.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • In-Role experience: 10+ years of experience in internal communications, corporate communications, or crisis management, with a proven track record operating at a principal or senior manager level within a global technology company.
  • Strategic partnership and execution: Demonstrated experience acting as a trusted right-hand to communications leadership, helping to steer broader program strategy while simultaneously executing on the ground.
  • Crisis & sensitive comms expertise: Deep, hands-on experience managing highly confidential and sensitive communications, particularly around M&A, restructuring, legal actions, and complex workplace issues.
  • Executive presence and discretion: Exceptional emotional intelligence, commanding poise under pressure, and the ability to interface with and influence C-suite executives and legal counsel on highly sensitive matters.
  • Project management: Very comfortable moving between strategic and tactical work, holding multiple projects to deadline, managing stakeholders, keeping partners informed, etc. Strong operational muscle to complement the strategic and creative work.
  • Ghostwriting range: Proven ability to write in the voice of a variety of leaders, often for people you don’t work with daily and with limited advance notice. Quick study on tone, cadence, and point of view.
  • Strategic excellence: Masterful storytelling and writing capabilities, with the ability to distill complex legal, regulatory, or organizational nuances into transparent, engaging, and culturally resonant employee communications.

Location

This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in San Francisco, CA, Oakland, CA, San Jose, CA, or the surrounding areas.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Compensation

*Please note this role is open to candidates outside of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, Washington D.C., and Washington State. The information below is provided for candidates hired in those locations only.

The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:

  • Based in Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Vermont or Washington D.C. : $141,520 - $176,900.
  • Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or California (outside of the San Francisco Bay area): $149,840 - $187,300.
  • Based in the San Francisco Bay area, California: $166,400 - $208,000.
  • This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan and corporate bonus plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Application deadline information (required for ALL US jobs)

Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until September 30, 2026, but may change based on business needs.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @ email address. jobs.title: (Senior) Google Ads Manager für AI-First Performance Marketing (m/w/d) · Remote
jobs.excerpt: Das ist dein Job bei unsBei der Analyse eines Google-Ads-Accounts fällt dir auf, dass ein Kunde mit einer Produktgruppe gar kein Geld verdient, obwohl der ROAS gut aussieht.
jobs.description:
Das ist dein Job bei uns

Bei der Analyse eines Google-Ads-Accounts fällt dir auf, dass ein Kunde mit einer Produktgruppe gar kein Geld verdient, obwohl der ROAS gut aussieht. Du gehst der Sache auf den Grund und stellst fest, dass die Marge dieser Gruppe deutlich schlechter ist als im Rest des Sortiments.

Du entwickelst eine neue Kampagnenstruktur, holst dir im Fachbereich noch zwei Impulse dazu und baust anschließend um. Das Reporting passt du gleich mit an.

Ein paar Tage später stellst du den neuen Aufbau dem Geschäftsführer des Unternehmens selbst vor. Er ist begeistert und du setzt mit Unterstützung aus dem EVOLVE Team um.

Eine Woche später fällt dir auf, dass du dieselbe Auswertung inzwischen zum dritten Mal manuell gebaut hast. Du sprichst mit Ali und Arthur aus unserem AI-Team und ihr automatisiert sie. Ab jetzt steht sie dem gesamten EVOLVE-Team auf Knopfdruck zur Verfügung.

Am Ende des Monats sind deine Kunden zufrieden, weil die Zahlen stimmen. Du hast viel gelernt und das EVOLVE-Team auch.

Genau das ist der Job.

Wofür wir arbeiten

Wir wollen der stärkste ganzheitliche Wachstumspartner für E-Commerce-Brands im DACH-Raum sein.

Denn was wir immer wieder sehen: Agenturen und Dienstleister betreuen Brands nischig und siloartig, Kanal für Kanal, ohne Blick aufs Ganze. Dabei bleiben enorme Potenziale auf der Strecke. Wir verstehen uns deshalb nicht als Dienstleister, sondern als Teil des Unternehmens unserer Kunden. Dafür arbeiten bei EVOLVE 30 Spezialisten in sechs Fachbereichen zusammen, vollständig remote und seit dem ersten Tag.

Wir denken Google Ads anders

Bei EVOLVE arbeiten wir daran, das reine Kampagnenmanagement so weit wie möglich an AI und Automatisierung zu übergeben. Nicht, um Menschen zu ersetzen, sondern um ihnen die Zeit für das zurückzugeben, was tatsächlich über Wachstum entscheidet:

  • Steuerung auf Deckungsbeitrag statt auf Kanal-Kennzahlen, die gut aussehen

  • Wachstumshebel jenseits des Google-Ads-Kontos wie Landingpages, Feeds, Angebotslogik und Funnel

  • Skalierung über YouTube, Display und Demand Gen, wo die meisten Wettbewerber gar nicht erst hinschauen

Genau dafür suchen wir jemanden.

Was dich hier erwartet

Du übernimmst nicht „ein paar Accounts". Du übernimmst Verantwortung für das Wachstum deiner Kunden im Google-Kanal, von der Analyse über die Strategie bis zur Umsetzung. Wie du dorthin kommst, entscheidest du. Denn wir werden nicht dafür bezahlt, Kampagnen zu verwalten. Wir werden dafür bezahlt, dass unsere Kunden wachsen: dass Budgets profitabel steigen, dass mehr Umsatz entsteht und am Ende mehr Profit übrig bleibt.

Was das im Alltag heißt:

  • Du steuerst und skalierst Google-Ads-Kampagnen profitabel über Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen und YouTube

  • Du erhöhst Budgets dort, wo sie profitabel wachsen, und erkennst die Grenzen, an denen es kippt

  • Du optimierst auf Deckungsbeitrag statt auf ROAS, weil unsere Kunden Geld verdienen wollen und keine Kennzahlen

  • Du führst deine Kunden strategisch und berätst eigenständig auf Entscheiderebene

  • Du arbeitest mit unserem internen AI-Stack für Analyse, Kampagnensteuerung und Reporting und entwickelst ihn mit weiter

  • Du bringst deine Erkenntnisse zurück ins Team und prägst mit, wie EVOLVE im Google-Kanal arbeitet

Der letzte Punkt ist uns wichtig. Was du herausfindest, bleibt nicht in deinem Account. Es wird Teil der Methodik, mit der das ganze Team arbeitet.

Das solltest du mitbringen

  • Mindestens zwei Jahre praktische Google-Ads-Erfahrung im E-Commerce, als Hauptkanal und nicht nebenbei

  • Analytisches Denken und schnelle Mustererkennung. Du siehst in Daten Zusammenhänge und nicht nur Zahlen

  • Die Bereitschaft, deine Arbeitsweise durch AI unterstützen zu lassen. Idealerweise probierst du dich bereits mit Skills, Skripten oder MCP-Connections aus

  • Sicherheit im direkten Kundenkontakt bis auf Geschäftsführungsebene

  • Sehr gute Selbstorganisation, denn bei 100 % Remote gibt es niemanden, der dich antreibt

Direkt gesagt: Dieser Job passt nicht zu jedem

Du solltest dich nicht bewerben, wenn dir Durchschnitt reicht. Wir tragen Entwicklung im Namen und meinen das ernst, fachlich, menschlich und in deiner Karriere. Du bist bei uns auch nicht richtig, wenn du Kunden nur oberflächlich betreuen möchtest oder rein im Silo-Denken innerhalb des Google-Ads-Kanals unterwegs bist.

Und nicht, wenn du AI für einen Hype hältst, den man aussitzen kann. Dafür ist hier der falsche Ort.

Der Rahmen

  • 100 % Remote seit Tag 1, kein Hybrid-Kompromiss

  • 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Jobrad und Firmenfitness über Wellpass

  • Laptop deiner Wahl und hochwertige Homeoffice-Ausstattung

  • Weiterbildungsbudget sowie Unterstützung durch interne und externe Quellen und Mentoren an deiner Seite

  • Voller Zugriff auf unseren internen AI-Stack

  • Zweimal jährlich Teamevents und Workations

So läuft der Prozess

  1. Deine Bewerbung. Dein Lebenslauf reicht. Wenn wir Rückfragen haben, schicken wir dir einen kurzen Fragebogen.

  2. Erstgespräch. Ein kurzes Video-Gespräch mit Vanessa aus unserem HR: gegenseitiges Kennenlernen, Rahmen und Erwartungen.

  3. Fachgespräch. Hier geht es in die Tiefe, mit der Geschäftsführung oder dem Lead deines Fachbereichs.

  4. Finales Kennenlernen. Mit der Geschäftsführung und deinem zukünftigen Ansprechpartner, persönlich und fachlich. Hier definieren wir deine Stelle noch einmal genau auf Basis deiner Stärken und Interessen.

  5. Entscheidung und Start. Wir entscheiden schnell und planen dein Onboarding gemeinsam.

Deine Entwicklung bei uns

Kurzfristig, die ersten zwei Monate. Du lernst unsere EVOLVE-Methodik kennen und arbeitest eng mit dem Team an ersten Projekten.

Mittelfristig. Du betreust eigene Projekte vollständig eigenständig und ganzheitlich. Google Ads ist dein Hauptfokus, aber du verstehst auch, welche Hebel über den Kanal hinaus für deine Kunden entscheidend sind.

Langfristig. Du machst bei uns Karriere, entweder in der Fachlaufbahn oder in der Führungslaufbahn. Beide Wege entstehen durch Ergebnisse und nicht durch Wartezeit.

Deine Ansprechpartnerin

Vanessa, unsere HR Managerin, ist dein erster Kontakt und freut sich auf deine Bewerbung.

Nice to Have

What Success Looks Like

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. It’s a short, self-recorded video that completes your application and allows hiring managers to get to know you before the interview process begins.

Rather than repeating your background during multiple screening calls, you’ll tell your story once, allowing future interviews to focus on meaningful conversations.

Don’t overthink it—you can record as many takes as you’d like before submitting. Your invitation will come from Spark Hire, so please check both your inbox and spam folder.

jobs.description:
Dental Insurance Specialist Position Summary

As part of our Dental Billing Services (DBS) team, the Insurance Specialist will provide Revenue Cycle Management to dental practices across the country by completing client-elected services such as claim submission, claim follow up, payment posting, and benefit verification with data entry.

Why does this role matter?
DBS provides revenue cycle management for dental practices across the country, so this person has a direct hand in whether our clients get paid accurately and on time. Claim submission, follow-up, payment posting, and benefit verification are the work that keeps a practice financially healthy and doing that work well is a big reason clients stay with us. It's a client-facing role at the center of how DentalXChange simplifies the business of dentistry.

What impact will the new hire have in their first 6 months?
The new hire will start as an Insurance Specialist, learning the DXC core values, our client relationships, and systems. Most importantly, they will learn how we deliver excellence daily, across all scopes of our services which impact our client experience. They will then move into an Account Manager role , where they own the client relationship, oversee the accuracy and timeliness of the work on their accounts, and deliver the monthly ROI reporting and Quarterly Business Reviews that our clients count on. By month six they should be the trusted point of contact for their book of accounts, helping onboard new clients, run audits, and bring newer team members up to speed.

What's the growth trajectory for this position?

Everything we build reflects our belief that finance should be thoughtfully crafted, fast, transparent, and frictionless.

Our Product & Regulatory Legal team operates like the rest of Mercury: with urgency, curiosity, and a bias toward action. We embed with product teams from early ideation through launch, working alongside engineers, designers, and compliance partners to get products right. We move fast, we take ownership, and we don't wait to be asked: If something needs figuring out, we’re up to the task.

  • Use AI intentionally: Bring a working knowledge of AI tools in legal workflows and a genuine interest in finding new ways to drive efficiency. We're building a legal team that works smarter, not just harder.
  • Be a storyteller: Translate dense regulatory concepts into straightforward, energizing narratives for product teams and other stakeholders as well as external audiences.
  • Stay curious and agile: Embrace each new regulation, market shift, or product pivot as a learning opportunity. Mercury's regulatory landscape is evolving quickly, and the scope of this role will grow with it. This is not a maintenance-only role.

What you should have:

  • 6+ years of legal experience, with at least 2 of those years focused on non-deposit investment products.
  • Familiarity with the Investment Advisers Act, Securities Act, Investment Company Act, Regulation Best Interest, Form CRS/ADV, FINRA rules, and related regulatory frameworks.

  • Exceptional communication skills. You know your audience and you tailor accordingly. You're as precise in a Slack thread as you are in a regulatory filing, and you know the value of a well-selected emoji in one versus the other.
  • A proactive sense of ownership. You're never afraid to say "I don't know, but I'll find out."
  • Strong working knowledge of AI use cases within legal roles and/or financial services generally and genuine interest in using AI to drive efficiency in your work.
  • Some additional experience outside the investments/brokerage space. The right candidate brings a broader foundation in financial services, payments, or fintech.

What will make you successful here:

Mercury is a place where legal counsel are expected to have a point of view. Not just about what the regulation requires, but about how the product can meet that bar in a way that's elegant, scalable, and good for customers. The people who thrive on this team treat ambiguity as an invitation rather than a reason to pause. They read a regulation and think about what it permits, not just what it prohibits.

You'll also spend a meaningful amount of your time on work that doesn't look like traditional legal practice: scoping cross-functional projects, pressure-testing product designs, building operational processes alongside compliance and ops partners. If you're someone who gets energy from that kind of work, and who measures their own impact by whether the product got better and not just whether the memo was airtight, you'll do well here.

Job Description:

Position Overview

RMI is seeking a Strategic Operations Analyst – Systems & Execution to support the day-to-day operation of core systems, processes, and reporting that enable effective project delivery, financial planning, and organizational decision-making.

This role sits within Strategic Operations and works across the Business Systems, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), and IT. The Analyst ensures that operational systems and workflows run smoothly, data is accurate and accessible, and teams are equipped to effectively use tools and reports.

Application Instructions

Please ensure you have read the entire job description before applying. In addition to your resume, please include a brief response to the following prompt:

Which part of this role most closely aligns with your prior experience, and which part would represent the steepest learning curve? Candidates who do not submit a response may not be considered.

Key Responsibilities

Systems Administration & Maintenance

  • Support the day-to-day administration of core operational systems, including Workday Projects Module, Adaptive Planning, and reporting tools (e.g., Power BI)

  • Assist with system updates, testing, and release management across Workday, Adaptive, and related tools

  • Troubleshoot system issues and escalate complex challenges to functional leads or IT partners

Process Execution & Operational Support

  • Support the execution of key operational workflows, to ensure financial and reporting readiness across business processes, including:

    • Project Budgeting and forecasting support (in partnership with FP&A)

    • Project Activation and reporting (in partnership with Business Systems)

    • Resource planning and utilization tracking

  • Support efforts to ensure processes are followed consistently and are as efficient as possible

User Support & Enablement

  • Serve as a first point of contact for user questions related to systems, reports, and processes, including monitoring the Projects Inbox.

  • Support staff on how to use systems and reports

  • Develop and maintain documentation, training materials, and user guides

  • Assist functional leads to support training sessions and improve data literacy across the organization

Cross-Functional Coordination & Continuous Improvement

  • Collaborate with Business Systems, FP&A, BI, and IT teams to support alignment across systems, data, and processes

  • Collaborate with the Workday/Adaptive architect, translating operational and reporting needs into system requirements

  • Support implementation of process improvements and system enhancements

  • Experience building or maintaining reports

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to support non-technical users

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working with enterprise systems (e.g., Workday, Adaptive Planning, or similar platforms)

  • Experience with BI tools such as Power BI or Tableau

  • Excellent Excel and data analysis skills; SQL or scripting experience a plus.

  • Exposure to project management, financial planning, or resource planning processes

  • Interest in systems, process improvement, and operational strategy

  • Mission-driven mindset and alignment with RMI’s values.

Please note: At this time, RMI is not able to sponsor employment visas or hire candidates who require visa sponsorship to work in the United States. All candidates must have current, independent authorization to work in the U.S. without present or future sponsorship from RMI. We will update our hiring pages if this status changes.

Location

We are a remote-ready company with team members around the globe. Our beautiful and welcoming offices are available for meetings or focused work, whether you are traveling through or living nearby. Our U.S. offices are in New York City; Washington DC; Oakland, California; Boulder, Colorado, and Basalt, Colorado. This role can be located from anywhere in the continental United States.

We provide you with the essential IT equipment plus a one-time home technology payment and a monthly work from home/commuter allowance to ensure you have a comfortable home office set up and necessary supplies.

At RMI, we prioritize fairness in our pay practices. Salaries are determined based on a mix of experience, market benchmarks, and internal equity across similar roles. In addition to base salary, this position includes an annual bonus target of 5% and eligibility for merit-based increases, which are tied to both individual and organizational performance.

We are hiring a Frontend Software Engineering Manager (Hands-On technical) to our Partners Acquisition team in Brazil!

The Partners Area is accountable for the supplier side of our marketplace, ensuring gym and wellness partners can seamlessly onboard and thrive. The Partners Acquisition team specifically owns the critical entry point of this ecosystem: the entire acquisition journey (self-sign-up funnels, referral systems, automated content setup, and system activation). Our ultimate goal is to drastically reduce time-to-market for new partners globally. To achieve this, we are a heavily data-informed squad that runs multiple parallel A/B tests to optimize every step of our conversion funnel.

  • Accelerate Global Onboarding: Lead the delivery of a highly optimized, high-conversion self-service product that eliminates onboarding friction for new B2B partners.

  • Lead a Blended Architecture: Successfully manage and architect a diverse ecosystem that seamlessly connects high-traffic frontend apps (Tanstack/React/TS) and backend services (Kotlin/AWS) with our core CRM/ERP data workflows (Salesforce).
  • Champion Engineering Excellence & AI: Establish modern SDLC standards, mandating and driving the adoption of AI-assisted development tools for faster coding, automated reviews, and testing.
  • Empower a Cross-Functional Team: Foster a high-performance culture across a hybrid squad of 6 engineers (4 Frontend, 2 Backend).

jobs.description:
From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.

​

During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Semantic Layer team in Bengaluru. You'll own the health, delivery, and growth of the team behind MetricFlow — building and coaching a group of engineers, setting technical direction in partnership with your leads, and ensuring one of the most important projects in the modern data stack keeps shipping with quality and momentum.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend most of your time growing people, running a healthy delivery process, and shaping strategy — but you'll stay close enough to the code and the architecture to make sound technical calls and earn the trust of a senior engineering team. You'll also be the steward of a public, community-facing open-source project, balancing the needs of internal roadmap and external contributors.

About the team

The Semantic Layer team owns the systems that turn dbt models into trusted, reusable business metrics. At the heart of this is MetricFlow — the open-source semantic engine that powers the dbt Semantic Layer. MetricFlow lets data teams define metrics once in code and consume them consistently across BI tools, notebooks, AI agents, and downstream applications.

This team is the steward of MetricFlow as an open-source project: shipping releases, reviewing community contributions, evolving the query compiler, and ensuring it integrates cleanly with the broader dbt ecosystem. The team works at the intersection of language design, query compilation, and distributed data execution — solving problems that directly shape how thousands of organizations measure their business.

What you'll do

  • Lead, coach, and grow a team of software engineers building MetricFlow — hiring, onboarding, career development, performance management, and day-to-day support.

  • Own delivery for the Semantic Layer team: planning, prioritization, execution, and predictable shipping of high-quality software.

  • Partner with your senior and staff engineers to set technical direction across metric definitions, query compilation, dimensional modeling, and SQL generation for multiple data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and others).

  • Steward MetricFlow as an open-source project — set the bar for how the team triages issues, reviews external pull requests, manages releases, and engages the community on GitHub and in Slack.

  • Collaborate with engineering leaders across the dbt platform, dbt Core, and the Semantic Layer service to ensure MetricFlow integrates seamlessly with the rest of the dbt ecosystem.

  • Partner with product, design, and developer-relations counterparts to translate customer and community feedback into a clear, well-sequenced roadmap.

  • Drive engineering excellence in performance, reliability, and observability of metric query execution at scale.

  • Foster a culture of design docs, thoughtful code review, and durable engineering — shipping fast without shipping sloppy.

Skills we're looking for

  • Experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, and performance management, with a track record of shipping production systems.

  • A strong engineering foundation — you've built and shipped production software yourself and can engage credibly on architecture and technical tradeoffs with a senior team.

    • Lead the design of scalable, data-driven marketing technology architectures that support both B2B and B2C customer journeys.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Impact
jobs.excerpt: JOB POSTINGSENIOR MANAGER, IMPACTABOUT THE CANADIAN PARALYMPIC COMMITTEEThe Canadian Paralympic Committee is a non-profit, private organization in collaboration with 28-member sport organizations.
jobs.description:
JOB POSTING

SENIOR MANAGER, IMPACT

ABOUT THE CANADIAN PARALYMPIC COMMITTEE

The Canadian Paralympic Committee is a non-profit, private organization in collaboration with 28-member sport organizations. We are deeply committed to harnessing the transformative power and impact of Paralympic sport.

With a vision of fostering an inclusive world through Paralympic sport, our mission emphasizes both the excellence in games preparation and the promotion of inclusive communities. By celebrating the stories and successes of high-performance athletes with disabilities, the Canadian Paralympic Committee aims to inspire all Canadians to embrace inclusivity and actively engage in sports.

Job summary

The Senior Manager, Impact will collaborate closely with the Chief Commercial & Impact Officer to develop and integrate CPC’s organization-wide impact practice, strengthening how initiatives are designed, delivered, measured and communicated, and how investment is translated into meaningful, measurable outcomes.

Supporting both the Canadian Paralympic Committee (CPC) and the Paralympic Foundation of Canada (PFC), the Senior Manager will serve as a key organizational connector. They will bring expertise in impact strategy, program design, measurement and storytelling to help teams strengthen existing initiatives, develop new opportunities and demonstrate the value created for athletes, people with disabilities, communities, partners and the sport system.

This is a strategic and hands-on role. The Senior Manager will lead CPC’s social value and impact measurement practice, strengthen a portfolio of priority initiatives, and help shape opportunities for corporate, philanthropic and government investment. They will also directly lead selected cross-functional initiatives and programs requiring dedicated ownership. Sitting within the Marketing & Communications team, the role will connect evidence with compelling stories and strengthen how CPC communicates its impact and influence.

Type: Full-time

Salary: $78,000- $90,000 annually plus benefits

Reports: Chief Commercial & Impact Officer

Location: Remote within Canada, with travel to CPC head office in Ottawa for occasional in-person meetings.

Main duties and responsibilities

Organization-wide impact leadership

  • Work alongside the CCIO to develop and integrate CPC’s organization-wide impact practice, establishing shared frameworks, capabilities and ways of working.
  • Maintain an organization-wide view of CPC’s impact portfolio and provide recommendations on priorities, sequencing, investment potential, risks, and capacity.
  • Work with program owners to strengthen intended outcomes, delivery models, measurements, and long-term sustainability. Help teams resolve barriers, connect related work, and integrate appropriate lived-experience advisory.
  • Directly lead selected cross-functional impact initiatives and partnerships requiring dedicated ownership.

Impact measurement, social value and learning

  • Lead the development and implementation of CPC’s impact measurement and social value practice. Align CPC’s approach with relevant national and international frameworks, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
  • Develop theories of change, outcomes, indicators, and practical evaluation plans for priority initiatives.
  • Establish proportionate processes for collecting, analyzing and reporting impact evidence with program owners, Finance and external partners.
  • Use evidence and learning to strengthen program design, inform investment decisions, and demonstrate individual, community and system-level change.

Impact reporting and knowledge mobilization

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of impact evidence and stories across CPC and PFC, covering programs, grants, athlete and participant experiences, partner contributions and broader system progress.
  • Work with Marketing & Communications to translate evidence into accessible and respectful stories, and support the development of CPC’s annual Impact Report, case studies, impact summaries and decision materials for partners, funders, government, the Board and members.
  • Translate research, evaluation findings and implementation learning into practical tools and recommendations for CPC and the broader sport system

Cross-functional leadership

  • Build trusted relationships across CPC and with external partners, creating clarity around responsibilities, decisions, timelines, and shared outcomes.
  • Lead planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting for assigned initiatives.
  • Manage consultants, researchers, and evaluation partners as required.
  • Represent CPC in selected working groups, consultations, and sector initiatives.
  • During Games and other major events, take on an assigned cross-functional role based on organizational priorities. This may include activating strategic initiatives, supporting stakeholders and community programming, or contributing to partner and government engagement.

Qualifications

  • Seven or more years of progressive experience in social impact, strategy implementation, program development, evaluation, partnerships, or related field.
  • Demonstrated experience strengthening complex initiatives and moving cross-functional work from concept through implementation.
  • Experience developing theories of change, outcome frameworks, indicators, and practical evaluation approaches.
  • Experience translating evidence and program results into clear reports, investment cases, and compelling stories.
  • Strong strategic thinking, project leadership, analytical writing, presentation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Experience influencing across teams and working with senior leaders, funders, corporate partners, community organizations and other complex stakeholder groups.
  • Relevant post-secondary education and/or equivalent professional experience.

The following are considered assets:

  • Experience developing impact-led partnerships or propositions for corporate, philanthropic or government investment.
  • Knowledge of accessibility, disability inclusion, the social model of disability, the UN Sustainable Development Goals, or social value measurement.
  • Experience working in sport and alongside athletes, people with disabilities or lived-experience advisors.
  • Bilingualism in English and French.

Personal profile

  • Strategic, practical, and focused on outcomes.
  • Comfortable moving between organization-wide priorities and detailed execution.
  • Proactive, resourceful, and able to create momentum in a complex environment.
  • Analytical and comfortable working with evidence, financial considerations, and human stories.
  • Collaborative and credible, with the ability to influence across teams.
  • Committed to accessibility, inclusion, social impact and the Paralympic Movement.

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Remote work environment, with the successful candidate working primarily from within Canada and attending the office as needed.
  • The CPC head office is currently located in Ottawa, Ontario.
  • Staff based outside Ottawa will be expected to travel to Ottawa a few times each year, or as required by the role.
  • Overnight and international travel, as well as off-site work, will be required for Games, site visits, events, and meetings.
  • Evening and weekend work will be required during busy periods, including Games and other special events.

APPLICATION PROCESS

If you share our passion for sport and are committed to CPC’s values, please submit your cover letter and résumé.

Please apply through BambooHR using the link provided.

Deadline to apply: August 14th, 2026 AT 5 PM EST

Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

CPC is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, record of offences, age, marital status, family status, or disability. We strongly encourage people from underrepresented or marginalized groups to apply.

CPC welcomes and encourages applications from First Nations, Métis, and Inuit peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, women, and/or 2SLGBTQ+ individuals. Accommodation is available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process

OFFRE D’EMPLOI

GESTIONNAIRE PRINCIPAL(E), IMPACT

À PROPOS DU COMITÉ PARALYMPIQUE CANADIEN

Le Comité paralympique canadien est un organisme privé sans but lucratif qui collabore avec 28 organismes de sport membres. Il est résolument déterminé à exploiter le pouvoir de transformation et la portée du sport paralympique.

Sa vision est de promouvoir le sport paralympique comme tremplin vers un monde inclusif. Sa mission met l’accent sur l’excellence lors de la préparation pour les Jeux, ainsi que sur la promotion de collectivités inclusives. En célébrant les parcours et les réussites des athlètes de haut niveau ayant un handicap, le Comité paralympique canadien souhaite inciter les Canadiennes et les Canadiens à adopter l’inclusion et à s’engager activement dans le sport.

Résumé des fonctions

La personne titulaire du poste de gestionnaire principal(e), Impact, travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le chef/la cheffe de la direction commerciale et de l’impact (CDCI), afin d’élaborer et d’intégrer une approche organisationnelle en matière d’impact au sein du Comité paralympique canadien (CPC). Elle contribuera ainsi à renforcer la conception, la mise en œuvre, l’évaluation et la communication des initiatives de l’organisation, ainsi qu’à transformer les investissements en résultats concrets, significatifs et mesurables.

Au service du CPC et de la Fondation paralympique canadienne (la Fondation), elle jouera un rôle clé de liaison au sein de l’organisation. Elle mettra à profit son expertise en stratégie d’impact, en conception de programmes, en mesure des résultats et en communication narrative afin d’aider les équipes à renforcer les initiatives existantes, à élaborer de nouvelles possibilités et à mettre en évidence la valeur créée pour les athlètes, les personnes en situation de handicap, les communautés, les partenaires et le système sportif.

Il s’agit d’un poste à la fois stratégique et concret. La personne titulaire dirigera les activités du CPC liées à la valeur sociale et à la mesure de l’impact, renforcera un portefeuille d’initiatives prioritaires et contribuera à définir des possibilités d’investissement pour les entreprises, les donatrices et donateurs, ainsi que les administrations publiques. Elle pilotera également certaines initiatives et certains programmes interfonctionnels nécessitant une responsabilité clairement attribuée. Relevant de l’équipe du marketing et des communications, la personne titulaire du poste fera le lien entre les données probantes et des récits convaincants, et renforcera ce faisant la façon dont le CPC communique son impact et son influence.

Type : Temps plein

Salaire : Salaire annuel de 78 000 à 90 000 $, plus avantages sociaux

Relève : Du chef/de la cheffe de la direction commerciale et de l’impact

Lieu : À distance, au Canada, avec des déplacements occasionnels au siège social du CPC, à Ottawa, pour des réunions en présentiel

Tâches et responsabilités principales

Leadership en matière d’impact à l’échelle de l’organisation

  • Collaborer avec le/la CDCI à l’élaboration et à l’intégration de la pratique du CPC en matière d’impact à l’échelle de l’organisation, notamment par la mise en place de cadres, de capacités et de méthodes de travail communs.
  • Maintenir une vue d’ensemble du portefeuille d’initiatives d’impact du CPC et formuler des recommandations quant aux priorités, à l’ordre de mise en œuvre, au potentiel d’investissement, aux risques et à la capacité organisationnelle.
  • Collaborer avec les responsables de programmes au renforcement des résultats visés, des modèles de prestation, des mesures et de la viabilité à long terme. Aider les équipes à surmonter les obstacles, à créer des liens entre les travaux connexes et à intégrer, lorsque cela est pertinent, les conseils de personnes ayant une expérience vécue.
  • Piloter directement certaines initiatives et certains partenariats interfonctionnels en matière d’impact nécessitant une prise en charge attitrée.

Mesure de l’impact, valeur sociale et apprentissage

  • Diriger l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la pratique du CPC en matière de mesure de l’impact et de valeur sociale. Harmoniser l’approche du CPC avec les cadres nationaux et internationaux pertinents, notamment les objectifs de développement durable des Nations Unies.
  • Élaborer des théories du changement, des résultats, des indicateurs et des plans d’évaluation concrets pour les initiatives prioritaires.
  • Établir, en collaboration avec les responsables de programmes, l’équipe des finances et les partenaires externes, des processus adaptés à l’envergure des initiatives pour recueillir, analyser et communiquer les données probantes sur l’impact.
  • Mettre à profit les données probantes et les apprentissages pour améliorer la conception des programmes, éclairer les décisions d’investissement et démontrer les changements à l’échelle des personnes, des collectivités et des systèmes.

Rapports sur l’impact et mobilisation des connaissances

  • Constituer et alimenter un flux continu de données probantes et de récits sur l’impact au sein du CPC et de la Fondation, portant notamment sur les programmes, les subventions, l’expérience des athlètes et des personnes participantes, les contributions des partenaires et les progrès réalisés à l’échelle du système.
  • Collaborer avec l’équipe du marketing et des communications afin de présenter les données probantes sous forme de récits accessibles et respectueux, et contribuer à la production du rapport annuel sur l’impact du CPC, d’études de cas, de synthèses sur l’impact et de documents d’aide à la décision destinés aux partenaires, aux bailleurs de fonds, aux gouvernements, au conseil d’administration et aux membres.
  • Transformer les résultats de recherche, les constats d’évaluation et les apprentissages tirés de la mise en œuvre en outils pratiques et en recommandations à l’intention du CPC et de l’ensemble du système sportif.

Leadership interfonctionnel

  • Établir des relations de confiance au sein du CPC et avec les partenaires externes, en veillant à clarifier les responsabilités, les décisions, les échéanciers et les résultats communs.
  • Diriger la planification, la budgétisation, les prévisions et la production de rapports pour les initiatives qui lui sont confiées.
  • Gérer les consultantes et consultants, les chercheuses et chercheurs, ainsi que les partenaires d’évaluation, au besoin.
  • Représenter le CPC au sein de certains groupes de travail, dans le cadre de consultations et lors d’initiatives sectorielles.
  • Pendant les Jeux et d’autres événements d’envergure, assumer un rôle interfonctionnel déterminé en fonction des priorités organisationnelles. Ce rôle peut notamment consister à mettre en œuvre des initiatives stratégiques, à soutenir les parties prenantes et les programmes communautaires, ou à contribuer aux relations avec les partenaires et les gouvernements.

Qualifications

  • Au moins sept ans d’expérience dans des fonctions aux responsabilités croissantes dans les domaines de l’impact social, de la mise en œuvre de stratégies, de l’élaboration de programmes, de l’évaluation, des partenariats ou dans un domaine connexe.
  • Expérience démontrée dans le renforcement d’initiatives complexes et dans la réalisation de projets interfonctionnels, de leur conception à leur mise en œuvre.
  • Expérience dans l’élaboration de théories du changement, de cadres de résultats, d’indicateurs et de méthodes d’évaluation concrètes.
  • Expérience dans la présentation de données probantes et de résultats de programmes sous forme de rapports clairs, d’argumentaires d’investissement et de récits convaincants.
  • Solides aptitudes pour la réflexion stratégique, la direction de projets, la rédaction analytique, les présentations et l’établissement de relations.
  • Expérience dans l’exercice d’une influence auprès de différentes équipes et dans la collaboration avec l’équipe dirigeante, des bailleurs de fonds, des partenaires commerciaux, des organismes communautaires et d’autres groupes complexes de parties prenantes.
  • Formation postsecondaire pertinente et/ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.

Les qualifications suivantes sont considérées comme des atouts :

  • Expérience dans l’élaboration de partenariats ou de propositions axés sur l’impact afin d’obtenir des investissements d’entreprises, d’organisations philanthropiques ou d’administrations publiques.
  • Connaissance des enjeux liés à l’accessibilité et à l’inclusion des personnes en situation de handicap, du modèle social du handicap, des objectifs de développement durable des Nations Unies ou des méthodes de mesure de la valeur sociale.
  • Expérience professionnelle dans le milieu sportif et auprès d’athlètes, de personnes en situation de handicap ou de conseillères et conseillers ayant une expérience vécue.
  • Bilinguisme (anglais-français)

Profil individuel

  • Esprit stratégique, sens pratique et souci d’obtenir des résultats.
  • Aptitude à passer des priorités organisationnelles aux détails de la mise en œuvre.
  • Esprit d’initiative, débrouillardise et capacité à faire avancer les projets dans un environnement complexe.
  • Esprit analytique et aisance à travailler avec des données probantes, des considérations financières et des récits humains.
  • Esprit de collaboration, crédibilité et capacité à exercer une influence auprès de différentes équipes.
  • Engagement envers l’accessibilité, l’inclusion, l’impact social et le mouvement paralympique.

CONDITIONS DE TRAVAIL

  • Environnement de travail à distance : le candidat retenu/la candidate retenue travaillera principalement depuis le Canada et se rendra au bureau si nécessaire.
  • Le siège social du CPC se situe actuellement à Ottawa, en Ontario.
  • Le personnel basé à l’extérieur d’Ottawa devra se rendre à Ottawa plusieurs fois par an ou selon les besoins liés au poste.
  • Des déplacements de plus de 24 heures et à l’étranger, ainsi que du travail hors site, seront nécessaires pour les Jeux, les visites de sites, les événements et les réunions
  • Il sera nécessaire de travailler les soirs et les fins de semaine lors des périodes chargées, notamment pendant les Jeux et lors d’autres événements spéciaux.

PROCESSUS DE DÉPÔT DES CANDIDATURES

Si vous partagez notre passion pour le sport et si vous adhérez aux valeurs du CPC, veuillez envoyer une lettre d’accompagnement et votre CV.

Veuillez déposer votre candidature par l’entremise de BambooHR en utilisant le lien fourni.

jobs.description:
Junior Commercial Litigation Barrister or Solicitor (Consultant)

We are looking for a junior Commercial Litigation Barrister or Solicitor to join Harper James on a flexible, freelance consultancy basis.

This is an excellent opportunity to support a growing and diverse client base, ranging from innovative start-ups and scale-ups to established national and international businesses. You will assist our litigation team with the preparation and progression of court proceedings within a modern, tech-enabled law firm.

Working as part of our flexible consultant model, you will have the autonomy to manage agreed workstreams while benefiting from the support, infrastructure and collaborative culture of a forward-thinking national firm.

What you’ll be doing

You will support senior members of the Commercial Litigation team with the preparation, management and conduct of court litigation.

The role will suit an organised and detail-focused lawyer who is confident handling procedural work, drafting, evidence preparation and case administration to a high standard.

Your work is likely to include:

  • Assisting with the preparation and drafting of statements of case, applications, witness statements, chronologies and other court documents

  • Conducting legal and factual research to support live disputes and litigation strategy

  • Reviewing, organising and analysing documentary evidence

  • Preparing trial bundles, hearing bundles and electronic bundles in accordance with court requirements

  • Assisting with disclosure exercises, including document review, categorisation and preparation of disclosure lists

  • Drafting correspondence with clients, opponents, counsel, courts and other relevant parties

  • Preparing case summaries, attendance notes, hearing notes and internal updates

  • Supporting the preparation of applications, hearings, mediations and trials

  • Assisting with the management of court deadlines, procedural timetables and case management requirements

  • Liaising with clients to obtain instructions, documents and witness evidence

  • Supporting senior solicitors and barristers with the efficient day-to-day management of litigation matters

You may also have the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across the wider Harper James legal team where disputes intersect with corporate, commercial, employment, intellectual property, real estate or insolvency matters.

What we’re looking for

A UK qualified Barrister or Solicitor with experience in commercial litigation and court procedure.

  • Junior-level experience, with the confidence to assist on active litigation matters under appropriate supervision

  • Strong knowledge of the Civil Procedure Rules and practical experience of litigation processes

  • Experience preparing court documents, bundles, chronologies and evidence

  • Excellent legal research, drafting and analytical skills

  • Strong attention to detail, particularly in relation to procedural requirements and document management

  • Ability to work efficiently, independently and flexibly while managing competing priorities

  • Clear and professional communication skills, both written and verbal

  • A pragmatic, client-focused approach and an interest in supporting ambitious businesses through dispute resolution

  • Experience working with electronic disclosure, e-bundling or litigation technology would be advantageous

The Harper James difference

We are a tech-driven, agile law firm where lawyers are empowered with modern legal technology to maximise efficiency, productivity and work-life balance. Our consultant model offers flexibility, autonomy and the ability to work remotely, while remaining part of a supportive national team.

At Harper James, we keep things straightforward. We are relaxed and informal but well organised.

There are no politics and no big egos, if people around us succeed, so do we. We welcome proactive, self-motivated lawyers who thrive in a modern legal environment and are passionate about delivering exceptional client service.

The bottom line

This is an opportunity to play an important role in supporting the continued growth of our Commercial Litigation team, working alongside experienced colleagues and a great team of people who all contribute to our shared success.

Flexible working within a fully remote but collaborative team. Ad hoc attendance at our office in the centre of Birmingham is likely from time-to-time depending on work requirements.

We are offering a competitive consultancy rate, with flexibility and autonomy as part of the Harper James consultant model.

NO AGENCIES PLEASE

The Nurse Practitioner is responsible to provide appropriate assessment and care to patients in a virtual clinic environment. The successful applicant works independently in diagnosing conditions, prescribing medications, performing, or ordering diagnostic tests and treatments, evaluating treatments, and providing follow-up care within the continuum of care. The Nurse Practitioner provides comprehensive and holistic nursing care to clients including health promotion, injury and illness treatment and prevention.

As an advanced practitioner, the Nurse Practitioner functions in the roles of practitioner, educator, and leader. As governed by provincial regulations, he/she practices independently, collaborating with other healthcare professionals including primary care physicians for issues outside the Nurse Practitioner scope of practice.

Essential Duties:

  • Coordinates treatment plans and follow up based on appropriate assessments, client and family response and outcomes, collaborating with other healthcare professionals if needed
  • Communicates findings and diagnosis to client and/or inter-professional team. Discusses prognosis, treatment options and outcomes with client and/or other team members within the circle of care and documents within the client's permanent health record
  • Advocates for clients, assessing their needs and if applicable, referring to appropriate care providers, professionals, or other services in the interest of the continuum of care
  • Follow best practice guidelines

Qualifications:

  • Current or willingness to obtain licensure as a Nurse Practitioner with the College of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador
  • Graduation from an approved School of Nursing
  • Preferred 1 year of recent experience as a practicing Nurse Practitioner preferred. Previous clinical experience will be considered
  • Experience working in emergency or urgent care considered an asset
  • Demonstrated knowledge of home and community health services
  • Family All Ages (FAA) is required
  • Experience practicing in a rural setting considered an asset
  • Exceptional clinical assessment and decision-making abilities
  • Demonstrated leadership qualities and problem-solving skills
  • Strong oral and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated ability to work well independently and in a collaborative team environment
  • Must have very strong computer and technology skills to be able to deliver virtual care through the use of technology

  • A commitment to professional development
  • A passion for telehealth and an advocate for the benefits and opportunities that telehealth offers to patients and clients
  • A satisfactory background screening result
  • You must have your own computer system with 2 monitors, USB headset, webcam, and high-speed internet connection to connect through VPN

We are flexible in offering either full time or part time and offer a competitive compensation package.

Why Work With Us

With over 20 years in the telehealth industry servicing clients across North America, Fonemed prides itself on providing outstanding client experience and practicing a culture of care in everything we do. We are a growing company who values our greatest resource - our people! We provide a collaborative company culture and a welcoming team. We offer our team the opportunity to work in an exciting industry and a competitive compensation package, including health benefits and retirement saving options, as well as a great paid leave program. If you are looking for an opportunity to work from home for a company that values you, apply today!

Fonemed is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to diversity. We appreciate the interest of everyone who applies for the position, however only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Please visit our website at www.fonemed.com.
